XIAN, China, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Bon Natural Life Limited (NASDAQ: BON) ("BON" or the "Company"), a leading provider of bio-ingredient solutions for the natural, health, and personal care industries, today announced that its subsidiary, Xi'an App-Chem Bio (Tech) Co., Ltd. ("App-Chem") recently convened a symposium with China Oat Group Co., Ltd. ("China Oat Group") on the theme of "Advancing the High-Quality Development of China's Health Industry". At the event, the two parties announced the establishment of the BON Natural Ingredients and Biomanufacturing Joint Laboratory (the "BON Joint Lab" or the "Joint Lab").

Through an innovative collaboration model, the BON Joint Lab aims to build an integrated innovation framework spanning the entire value chain, from fundamental research and pilot-scale development to standard-setting and industrial commercialization. The Joint Lab will focus on developing an AI-driven technological platform for the biomanufacturing of natural ingredients, with synthetic biology serving as its technological foundation and artificial intelligence (AI) as a key competitive differentiator. Its primary focus will be the development of biomanufacturing technologies for high-value natural ingredients. This integrated technological framework is expected to enhance the Joint Lab's competitive position in the natural ingredients biomanufacturing sector while offering the industry new alternatives to conventional production methods.

Oats are widely recognized for their nutritional value and health benefits. They contain bioactive compounds such as beta-glucan and avenanthramides (AVAs), which have demonstrated various biological activities, including cardiovascular protection, blood glucose regulation, antioxidant effects, and anti-inflammatory properties. As a supplier of oat-based health products, China Oat Group serves a market characterized by strong demand and significant growth potential. However, limited availability of natural raw materials and high sourcing costs have constrained the broader commercial application and market expansion of oat-derived products.

Through the establishment of the Joint Lab, BON and China Oat Group aim to develop biomanufacturing technologies for oat-derived natural ingredients, with the goal of fundamentally addressing challenges related to supply availability, supply stability, and high production costs. BON and China Oat Group believe that this initiative is of significant importance in expanding the market for oat-derived natural ingredients.

Standards development plays a critical role in the biomanufacturing of natural ingredients. The unique complexity of natural ingredient sourcing, heightened regulatory scrutiny of product safety, and distinct consumer preferences for naturally derived ingredients make the establishment of standards for biomanufactured natural ingredients critically important to their commercial value.

BON and China Oat Group have undertaken extensive and productive work in developing quality standards for natural ingredients. The Joint Lab will make standards development a dedicated area of focus, conducting systematic testing and validation of key parameters, including ingredient purity, safety, and elemental and isotopic profiles. Through a comprehensive and integrated process of evaluation and optimization, the Joint Lab aims to establish systematic differentiation in product standards across multiple dimensions, including safety, differentiated quality standards, and similarity to naturally derived counterparts.

BON has established a strong presence in the natural ingredients biomanufacturing sector and has articulated its vision of becoming an "AI-driven pioneer in digital nutrition". The Company is committed to accelerating the transition from conventional natural extraction methods to AI-driven biomanufacturing. The Company believes that it has built a strong technological foundation in natural products, biosynthesis, and the application of AI in biology, supported by robust industrialization capabilities and global market development expertise.

China Oat Group has developed extensive expertise across the entire oat value chain and holds more than ten invention patents in China, along with multiple patents in the United States, Europe, Canada, Australia, and other markets. Leveraging its advanced technologies in areas such as oat protein enzymatic hydrolysis and the preservation of beta-glucan bioactivity, China Oat Group has developed a portfolio of oat-based nutritional products whose health benefits have been evaluated through medical research. China Oat Group was also among the first companies to achieve large-scale, standardized deep processing of oats, with its related technologies receiving authoritative certifications in Europe and the United States.

Mr. Yongwei Hu, Chairman of BON, commented, "Our strategic collaboration with China Oat Group marks a pivotal step in our efforts to establish a stronger presence in the core natural ingredients sector, accelerate our expansion into the rapidly growing global biomanufacturing market, and further strengthen our position as an innovation leader in the industry. Through the Joint Lab, we aim to advance cutting-edge research in areas such as the biosynthesis of high-value natural ingredients, the discovery of functional bioactive compounds, and precision nutrition interventions. We are committed to accelerating the commercialization of scientific and technological innovations and delivering a broader range of safe and effective health solutions to consumers. Through the disciplined execution of our technology-driven business strategy, we seek to unlock significant commercial value and generate sustainable returns for our investors."

Under BTT’s most recent Repurchase Program, which ends November 30, 2026, the Trust could repurchase up to 5% of its outstanding common shares in open market transactions. Pursuant to the Boards’ authorization for BTT and BMN of their respective Repurchase Programs, each fund may repurchase up to 5% of its outstanding common shares (based on common shares outstanding on November 30, 2026) through November 30, 2027.

The Repurchase Programs seek to enhance shareholder value by purchasing Trust shares trading at a discount to each Trust’s net asset value (“NAV”) per share, which could result in incremental accretion to a Trust’s NAV. NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Peloton Interactive, Inc. (“Peloton”) (NASDAQ: PTON) today announced it has successfully completed a global refinancing that reduced overall debt and extended debt maturities.

Summary of Transactions

  • Peloton raised $700 million from new and existing investors through an upsized private offering of senior secured notes due 2032 (the “notes”).
  • Peloton entered into a new $200 million five-year revolving credit facility led by Goldman Sachs, which replaced Peloton’s existing $100 million five-year revolving credit facility.
  • Peloton repaid all term loans outstanding under its existing $1 billion five-year term loan facility and terminated the facility.

Peloton used the net proceeds from the offering of the notes, together with cash on hand, to repay all term loans outstanding under its existing $1.0 billion five-year term loan facility, which was terminated in connection with such repayment, and to pay fees and expenses related thereto.

“This transaction is a direct reflection of the progress we have made in strengthening Peloton’s financial foundation”, said Sid Thacker, Peloton’s Chief Financial Officer. “In addition to lower interest expense, we now have the flexibility to pursue our strategic ambitions and provide strong returns to our stakeholders in FY2027 and beyond.”

Peloton worked with its lead bank, Goldman Sachs, and its financial advisor, BDT & MSD Partners, to complete this holistic refinancing.

PHILADELPHIA, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Board of Trustees of abrdn Income Credit Strategies Fund (NYSE: ACP) has approved a 1-for-4 reverse stock split of the Fund's issued and outstanding common shares, effective prior to the opening of trading on December 7, 2026.

The Board approved the reverse stock split to increase the Fund's per-share market price. The Board believes a higher share price may reduce certain trading and administrative frictions associated with lower-priced securities, increase the Fund's suitability for certain investment platforms and intermediary programs, and better align the Fund's share price with industry trading conventions.

The aggregate value of a shareholder's investment is not expected to change solely as a result of the reverse stock split, although the market value of Fund shares will continue to fluctuate based on market conditions.

Under the terms of the transaction, every four common shares will be consolidated into one common share. No fractional shares will be issued; fractional share entitlements will be aggregated and sold, with the net proceeds distributed to affected shareholders. The transaction will apply equally to all shareholders and will not affect any shareholder's proportionate ownership interest, other than minor adjustments resulting from the treatment of fractional shares.

Russian Sanctions Developments

Due to the ongoing Russian war with Ukraine, the United Kingdom (the “U.K.”), the European Union (“E.U.”), the United States (“U.S.”) and other countries and organizations have publicly announced and enacted extensive sanctions against Russia to impose severe economic pressure on the Russian economy and government.

Two of our vessels, the Yenisei River and Lena River (the “Vessels”), are employed by Yamal Trade Pte. Ltd. (the “Charterer”) under long-term time charters that extend to 2033 and 2034, respectively (the “Yamal Charters”). Since the commencement of the Yamal Charters, the Vessels have been engaged in the transportation of LNG produced in Russia for discharge at destinations worldwide (the “Yamal LNG Transportation”) in compliance with applicable sanctions regulations.

U.K. Sanctions

On May 20, 2026, the Russia (Sanctions) (EU Exit) (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/543) came into force in the U.K., amending the Russia (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019. The amendments introduced new Regulations 46Z29B to 46Z29D, which prohibit U.K. persons from directly or indirectly supplying or delivering Russian-origin LNG by ship, and from providing or facilitating related services. The ban covers shipments from Russia to third countries as well as between third countries and is subject to limited exceptions and licensing arrangements. For supply contracts with a duration exceeding one year that were executed before June 17, 2025 and have not since been amended, other than by amendments falling within specified categories, there is a transitional exception that covers relevant activities carried out before January 1, 2027.

As a result, following expiry of the applicable transitional exception, U.K.-based providers of financial services, including the insurers that currently provide protection and indemnity (“P&I”) and hull and machinery (“H&M”) insurance for the Vessels, will be prohibited from providing cover for voyages carrying Russian-origin LNG, unless an applicable exception or licence permits such cover. The U.K. prohibition does not extend to technical services, including classification.

As of the date of this press release, discussions with alternative insurance providers are ongoing; however, we have not secured replacement P&I or H&M insurance for the Vessels and there can be no assurance that such insurance will be in place by January 1, 2027, or that it will be available on comparable terms, or at all. If such insurance is not in place, this could give rise to disputes under the Yamal Charters, including disputes concerning the respective rights and obligations of the Charterer and us under the Yamal Charters. Any such dispute could result in claims that the Vessels are off-hire, additional costs, loss of revenue, litigation or early termination of the Yamal Charters, among other things. Any of these developments could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows and our ability to make distributions to our unitholders and could result in an event of default under our debt agreements, among other things.

E.U. Sanctions

On October 23, 2025, the E.U. adopted the 19th package of sanctions (the “19th Package”), which prohibits the purchase, import or transfer, directly or indirectly, by E.U. persons and non-E.U. persons with an E.U.-nexus, of LNG that originates in Russia or is exported from Russia (the “LNG Prohibition”). The LNG Prohibition applies from January 1, 2027 with respect to supply contracts with a duration exceeding one year (“Long Term Contracts”) that were executed before June 17, 2025 and that have not since been amended, other than by amendments falling within specified categories.

On July 23, 2026, the E.U. amended the 19th Package with the adoption of the 21st package of sanctions (the “21st Package”). The 21st Package introduced an exemption to the LNG Prohibition, initially until July 25, 2027, and thereafter for successive periods of one year, unless the Council of the E.U. (the “E.U. Council”), following an annual review, decides otherwise. The exemption applies to transfers of LNG destined for third countries and, where relevant, purchases associated with those transfers, pursuant to Long Term Contracts that were executed before February 24, 2022 and that have not since been amended, other than by amendments falling within specified categories, provided that the volume of LNG transferred each year under the exemption does not exceed the volume of LNG transferred in 2025 under its qualifying existing Long Term Contract, irrespective of destination (the “Legacy Contract Derogation”).

We, and our sanctions counsel, believe that the transportation of LNG under the Yamal Charters to destinations outside the E.U. currently falls within the Legacy Contract Derogation and, accordingly, is outside the scope of the LNG Prohibition. However, there can be no absolute guaranteed assurance that our interpretation of the Legacy Contract Derogation is correct, or that regulatory authorities or our counterparties will agree with our interpretation. Furthermore, there can be no absolute guaranteed assurance that the transportation of LNG under the Yamal Charters will continue to meet the requirements of the Legacy Contract Derogation, including with respect to the yearly volume limitation, or that the E.U. Council will not decide, following an annual review, to shorten or terminate the Legacy Contract Derogation, or that sanctions regulations will not be further implemented, amended, or expanded to restrict the transportation of Russian-origin LNG.

These risks are outside of our control, and if one or more of these events were to occur, the Vessels would be restricted from transporting LNG originating in or exported from Russia, which would affect the Charterer’s ability to continue employing the Vessels in the Yamal LNG Transportation. Notwithstanding the foregoing, we believe the Yamal Charters would remain enforceable, although their sanctions-specific provisions may suspend performance and, at a later stage, payment of charter hire. The Charterer may not agree with our interpretation, which could result in disputes, Charterer non-performance, litigation or early termination of the Yamal Charters, among other things. Any of these developments would have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition, cash flows and our ability to make distributions to our unitholders and could result in an event of default under our debt agreements, among other things.

U.S. Sanctions

On September 18, 2026, the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (the “Graham Act”) was enacted in the U.S. Among other things, the Graham Act authorizes the President to impose sanctions on foreign vessels that the President determines knowingly transport LNG or certain other energy products originating in Russia, and on persons that provide services to such vessels. On October 16, 2026, the President issued Executive Order 14436, which waived the application of the sanctions, restrictions and duties provided for in the Graham Act. The waiver has no fixed expiration date, and it may be revoked or modified at any time. No sanctions have been imposed on us or the Vessels under the Graham Act. However, there can be no assurance that the waiver will remain in effect, or that sanctions will not be imposed under the Graham Act on us, the Vessels, the Charterer or our service providers, which could restrict or prevent the employment of the Vessels under the Yamal Charters and affect our access to insurance, financing and other services.

General

Our fleet consists of only six LNG carriers and we derive all our revenues from a limited number of charterers. For the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, the Charterer accounted for approximately 34% of our total revenues, and the charter revenue expected to be generated by the Yamal Charters constituted approximately 56% of our estimated contract backlog. The loss of revenue under either or both of the Yamal Charters would have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition, cash flows and our ability to make distributions to our unitholders, and could result in an event of default under our debt agreements.

The Company is actively pursuing the development of its nPulse technology for use in the treatment of atrial fibrillation and in a select few other markets where it could have a profound positive impact on healthcare for both patients and providers.

Consideration to 1847 Holdings is expected to include cash at closing, a senior seller note, a junior seller note, warrants and a performance-based adjustment. “We believe this transaction is a strong outcome for 1847 Holdings and its shareholders,” said Ellery W. Roberts, CEO of 1847 Holdings. “It is expected to significantly strengthen our balance sheet by allowing us to satisfy our outstanding debt obligations through the cash proceeds and senior seller note, while the junior seller note, warrants and performance-based adjustment provide our shareholders with the opportunity to benefit from CMD’s future growth. We are also pleased that CMD will become an employee-owned company, which we believe will give its team an even greater stake in the success of the business. Once the transaction is complete, we will be able to focus more on our other businesses, including Wolo, where revenue more than doubled in the third quarter as we continued shifting the business to e-commerce.”

Key Terms

descending-price clock auctiontechnical
A descending-price clock auction is a multi-round auction where the seller announces a starting price and then repeatedly lowers that price (the “clock”) while bidders publicly state how many units they would buy at each price. The process stops when total stated demand is less than or equal to the quantity offered; the auction clears at the final price and the available units are allocated, typically pro rata among bidders if demand still exceeds supply at the stopping price. Because bidders see aggregate demand as the price moves, the format reveals price sensitivity over time and prevents winners from paying more than the clearing level.

BRUSSELS, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Verlinvest S.A. ("Verlinvest"), an international, family-backed evergreen investment company, today announced that it has commenced a tender offer to purchase all of the outstanding ordinary shares, quota value SEK 0.0015 per share (the "Shares"), and all of the outstanding American Depositary Shares, each representing twenty Shares (the "ADSs" and, together with the Shares, the "Offer Securities") of Oatly Group AB (publ) (Nasdaq: OTLY), a public limited liability company organized under the laws of Sweden ("Oatly" or the "Company") in exchange for $0.2065 per Share (that is not represented by an ADS) or $4.13 per ADS, as applicable, in cash, without interest and subject to any applicable withholding taxes upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Offer to Purchase for Cash dated November 20, 2026 (the "Offer to Purchase") and in the related Letter of Transmittal for ADSs (the "ADS Letter of Transmittal") and Acceptance Form for Shares (the "Acceptance Form for Shares" which, together with the Offer to Purchase, the ADS Letter of Transmittal and other related materials, as each may be amended or supplemented from time to time, collectively constitute the "Offer").

The ADSs are listed on the NASDAQ Global Select Market ("Nasdaq") under the symbol "OTLY", and the Shares are not listed on any exchange (but if at least 20 Shares are held, multiples of 20 shares may be deposited with the depositary bank for the ADSs and exchanged for ADSs that are listed on Nasdaq). On November 19, 2026, the business day prior to the launch of the Offer, the closing price of the ADSs as reported on Nasdaq was $7.17 per ADS, equivalent to $0.3585 per underlying Share. The offer consideration of $0.2065 per Share or $4.13 per ADS, as applicable, represents a discount of approximately 42.4% to the November 19, 2026 closing price, a discount of 59.4% to the volume-weighted average closing price of the ADSs as quoted on Nasdaq over the three months prior to the date on which the Offer was launched, which was $10.18 and a discount of 61.5% to the volume-weighted average closing price of the ADSs as quoted on Nasdaq over the six months prior to the date on which the Offer was launched, which was $10.74.

ACCORDINGLY, THE OFFER CONSIDERATION IS SUBSTANTIALLY BELOW THE MARKET PRICE OF THE ADSs, AND VERLINVEST RECOMMENDS THAT HOLDERS OF ADSs AND SHARES NOT ACCEPT THE OFFER AND NOT TENDER THEIR SHARES OR ADSs IN THE OFFER.

VERLINVEST DOES NOT BELIEVE THAT THE OFFER IS FAIR, FROM A FINANCIAL POINT OF VIEW, TO THE SECURITY HOLDERS OF OATLY. VERLINVEST RECOMMENDS THAT SECURITY HOLDERS OF OATLY NOT ACCEPT THE OFFER AND NOT TENDER THEIR SHARES OR ADSs IN THE OFFER.

The Offer is being made solely to comply with the requirements of the Swedish Stock Market (Takeover Bids) Act (2006:451) (the "Swedish Statute") in connection with Verlinvest's proposed acquisition of the indirect interest held by its joint venture partner, Blossom Key (Hong Kong) Holdings Limited ("Blossom Key"), an indirect subsidiary of China Resources Enterprise, Limited ("China Resources"), in the Oatly securities held by Nativus Company Limited ("Nativus"), which is Oatly's largest shareholder. Each of Verlinvest and Blossom Key holds 50% of the issued shares of CR Verlinvest Health Investment Limited ("CRVV"), which holds, inter alia, all issued shares of Nativus. As of the date of the Offer to Purchase, Nativus holds 271,763,953 Shares, equal to 42.6% of the issued and outstanding Shares (excluding treasury shares) as of November 6, 2026, the latest practicable date prior to the date of the Offer to Purchase, and $209,278,211 aggregate principal amount of the Company's 9.25% Convertible Senior PIK Notes due 2028 (the "Convertible Notes"). Verlinvest wishes to acquire Blossom Key's 50% indirect interest in the Shares and the Convertible Notes held by Nativus and to directly hold all of the Shares and Convertible Notes held by Nativus.

An acquisition by Verlinvest of the Shares currently held by Nativus other than through a voluntary tender offer would trigger the mandatory tender offer requirements of the Swedish Statute, which requires any person who acquires 30% or more of the voting interests of all Shares to make a tender offer to purchase all outstanding Shares and ADSs held by all holders of Shares and ADSs in accordance with certain specific rules. Following consultation between Verlinvest and the Swedish Securities Council, the Swedish Securities Council has in two statements confirmed that Verlinvest may conduct a voluntary tender offer and acquire the Shares held by Nativus through such voluntary tender offer as an alternative to conducting a mandatory tender offer pursuant to the Swedish Statute.
